confirmed.title: Late-evidence obligation cannot be closed: resolution TP fills re-latch LATE_EVIDENCE and the audit never clears the invariant violation
confirmed.requirement: NG-CELL-003 (a late fill creates a new TP obligation of the old cycle, closed by TP), NG-HIST-002 (freeze until audit), AC-08, AC-42 (ledger part), NG-CELL-001
confirmed.failure_scenario: BUY cell, gen0 entry fills 4, is proven terminal (4), TP 4 fills and is proven, cycle released. A late history fill of 1 on the gen0 entry correctly returns LATE_EVIDENCE. The operator acknowledges it (acknowledge_late_evidence(0)) and a resolution TP of 1 is dispatched for gen0. When that TP fills normally, apply_fill returns LATE_EVIDENCE again and sets cycle.late_evidence=True, because `late = leg.is_final or cycle.closed` (cells.py:586) treats every fill on a released cycle as late, including fills of a TP created after the audit. Per handoff item 4, the engine freezes again, and every partial fill of the resolution TP needs another audit. acknowledge_late_evidence (cells.py:621-629) also leaves terminal_cumulative=4 with filled=5, and leaves a REJECTED_* leg with fills unchanged. So check_invariants (cells.py:681-685) reports 'gen0 ENTRY#0: filled 5 != terminal cumulative 4' (or 'rejected leg has fills') for the whole life of the ledger. Trace open-risk #4 says the engine must freeze on check_invariants(), so the market is frozen permanently after any late evidence, and no ledger API can repair it.
confirmed.evidence: Probe against the extracted commit c2b7c6ed9: late: LATE_EVIDENCE -> ack -> 'invariants after ack: [gen0 ENTRY#0: filled 5 != terminal cumulative 4]' -> resolution TP (1) -> 'resolution fill outcome: FillOutcome.LATE_EVIDENCE late flag True' -> next_entry_identity raises 'cycle 0 has late evidence/obligation (audit)' -> after a second ack the invariant error is still present. The worktree has an uncommitted fix for exactly this (late = leg.is_final only; the ack sets TERMINAL/terminal_cumulative=filled), but it is not in c2b7c6ed9 and no committed test covers the resolution path.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Treat only fills on already-final legs as late (`late = leg.is_final`). In acknowledge_late_evidence, turn the audited leg into TERMINAL with terminal_cumulative = filled (including REJECTED_* legs that executed) and record that correction durably. Add a committed test for the full late-evidence -> audit -> resolution TP -> release cycle.

verdict.reasoning:
The defect is real at c2b7c6ed9. I read the committed `cells.py` with `git show c2b7c6ed9:...` and ran a probe script against that exact file, using the test helpers, `contracts.py` and `grid.py`, which are unchanged since that commit.

What the committed code does:
- `cells.py:586` has `late = leg.is_final or cycle.closed`.
- `acknowledge_late_evidence` (`cells.py:621-629`) only clears the flags. It leaves `terminal_cumulative` alone and does not change REJECTED_* legs that have fills.
- `confirm_terminal` returns DUPLICATE or CONFLICT for a leg that is already TERMINAL. So no ledger API can change `terminal_cumulative` after the audit.

Probe output, following the claimed scenario (BUY cell, Q=10, rules with min_base=1):
- Entry fills 4 and is proven TERMINAL(4). The TP fills 4 and is proven TERMINAL(4). Release returns 0.
- A late fill of 1 on the entry returns LATE_EVIDENCE. `check_invariants` then reports `['gen0 ENTRY#0: filled 5 != terminal cumulative 4']`.
- After `acknowledge_late_evidence(0)` the same invariant error is still there.
- The dispatch plan gives a resolution TP of 1 for gen0. Its normal fill returns LATE_EVIDENCE and sets `cycle.late_evidence=True` again. `next_entry_identity` then raises "cycle 0 has late evidence/obligation (audit)".
- After a second acknowledgement, a new entry is possible, but `check_invariants` still reports the terminal-cumulative mismatch.

Why this breaks the spec:
- AC-08 says a late history fill "increases the obligation and is covered by TP".
- NG-CELL-003 says a late fill creates a new TP obligation of the old cycle.
- NG-HIST-002 and AC-42 say to freeze until audit.
- In this commit, each fill of the TP that pays off that obligation is itself reported as LATE_EVIDENCE. The trace's handoff item 4 maps LATE_EVIDENCE to FROZEN, so every partial fill of the resolution TP needs another operator audit.
- Trace open-risk #4 says the engine must freeze on `check_invariants()`. The mismatch never clears, so under that contract the market can never leave the freeze.
- The only committed test (`test_late_fill_after_release_goes_to_old_cycle_and_requires_audit`) stops at the first LATE_EVIDENCE. Nothing tests the audit, resolution TP and release path.

Mitigating points:
- The same branch fixes exactly this in later commit b5cd6c292 (now HEAD 09c29d8a4 is ahead of it). That commit changes the check to `late = leg.is_final`, makes acknowledge turn audited legs into TERMINAL with `terminal_cumulative=filled`, and adds tests. The finding therefore applies to the reviewed commit c2b7c6ed9, not to the branch tip.
- I lowered severity to medium. The failure is fail-closed: repeated or permanent freeze and a liveness loss, with no over-exposure or wrong order. The trigger is rare, a fill that arrives after the settlement window.
- The claim's wording "no ledger API can repair it" slightly overstates the lock. After a second ack a new entry is allowed. What persists is the invariant violation, and the engine contract turns that into a permanent freeze.

confirmed.title: TP headroom planner declares RISK_BLOCKED when the only same-side entries are SUBMIT_UNKNOWN (could still be cancelled)
confirmed.requirement: NG-RISK-002 (RISK_BLOCKED only when the cap is still incompatible after same-side pending entries are cancelled; otherwise cancel and wait for history terminal)
confirmed.failure_scenario: The cap is 20 and P_max is 20 because of a same-side BUY entry of 20 in SUBMIT_UNKNOWN (for example after a restart, when mark_intents_unknown ran, or after a timeout). A BUY TP of 10 needs headroom. plan_tp_headroom counts only CANCEL_IN_FLIGHT entries as in_flight and only LIVE/INTENT entries as candidates, so SUBMIT_UNKNOWN entries count as unfreeable: freeable 0 < excess 10, so risk_blocked. The router emits BLOCKED (router.py:226-232) and the engine goes to operator-required RISK_BLOCKED, although the entry will resolve to LIVE (then cancellable) or to a zero-fill reject (then freed). The same input with the entry LIVE gives CANCEL + WAIT.
confirmed.evidence: Probe on c2b7c6ed9: plan_tp_headroom(ep(P_max=20), BUY, 10, [OpenLeg(BUY, 20, ENTRY, SUBMIT_UNKNOWN)], cap 20) -> risk_blocked=True 'entries free 0'. plan_submits returns BLOCKED for the SUBMIT_UNKNOWN entry, and CANCEL 'u' + WAIT for the same order in LIVE.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Count same-side SUBMIT_UNKNOWN entry remainders as freeable-pending, like in-flight entries, and return WAIT. Return RISK_BLOCKED only when confirmed position plus non-entry orders alone exceed the cap.

verdict.reasoning:
The claim holds at c2b7c6ed9. risk.py and router.py are the same at HEAD 09c29d8a4.

**What the code does.** In risk.py:241-242, `plan_tp_headroom` counts only CANCEL_PENDING, CANCEL_UNKNOWN and TERMINAL_UNKNOWN entries as in_flight (`CANCEL_IN_FLIGHT_STATES`, risk.py:36). It takes only LIVE or INTENT entries as candidates (`CANCELLABLE_STATES` and `WITHDRAWABLE_STATES`, risk.py:32-34). A same-side SUBMIT_UNKNOWN entry is therefore in neither group and adds nothing to freeable, yet its full remainder is still inside P_max.

**Probe result.** I ran a probe with cap 20, ep P=0 / P_max=20, a BUY TP of 10 and one BUY entry of 20:
- SUBMIT_UNKNOWN gives `RISK_BLOCKED:BUY TP 10 needs 10, entries free 0`, and `plan_submits` emits `ActionKind.BLOCKED` (router.py:226-232).
- The same order as LIVE gives CANCEL 'u' + WAIT.
- As INTENT it gives WITHDRAW + WAIT.
- As CANCEL_PENDING it gives WAIT.

**Why this violates the spec.** NG-RISK-002 says the router cancels pending same-side entries, then waits for history terminal. RISK_BLOCKED (operator required) is allowed only "если cap всё равно несовместим с обязательством" ("if the cap is still incompatible with the obligation"). A SUBMIT_UNKNOWN entry is a pending entry whose remainder can still be released:
- It can resolve to REJECTED_ZERO_FILL.
- It can resolve to LIVE and then be cancelled.
- cells.py:63 even allows SUBMIT_UNKNOWN -> CANCEL_PENDING.

So incompatibility has not been established at that point. The workstream's own trace (ws-a-core.md, "Router semantics") says "SUBMIT_UNKNOWN and cancel-in-flight orders are waited for". The self-trade path does exactly that (test_router.py::test_unsent_entry_intent_is_withdrawn_unknown_submit_is_only_waited_for). The headroom path contradicts that design.

**Reachability.** An excess only appears with an external cause, such as a cap reduction. `max_abs_net_position` is not in `config_fingerprint` (grid.py:345-362), so it can be lowered across a restart. A restart is exactly when `mark_intents_unknown` turns INTENT entries into SUBMIT_UNKNOWN (handoff WS-D item 6). A transport timeout during a hard-risk or cap conflict reaches the same state. The handoff maps BLOCKED to the engine's RISK_BLOCKED state, which the spec says needs an operator. So a case that should be CANCEL/WAIT forces operator intervention and delays the TP exit.

**Impact.** It fails safe: no cap is exceeded and nothing is market-closed. The problem is liveness and a wrong state, so severity stays low.

confirmed.title: _split_valid chunks greedily by max_base and creates DUST when an exact valid split exists
confirmed.requirement: NG-GRID-003 (DUST only when the exact remainder is below the runtime minimum; no silent resize), AC-34 (runtime rule change must not create an unfillable TP when a valid one exists)
confirmed.failure_scenario: Q=10 entry accepted under max_base=None, fully filled and proven terminal. Runtime rules then change to max_base=6 (min_base 5, step 1). _split_valid takes chunk=min(10, 6)=6, leaving 4 < 5, so the TP plan is (6,) with DUST 4 and the cell is locked. The exact split 5+5 is valid under the new rules. dust.aggregate (dust.py:108) behaves the same way: it skips the whole group when the total exceeds max_base instead of forming a valid aggregate at or below max_base.
confirmed.evidence: Probe on c2b7c6ed9: tp_obligation_to_dispatch(rules(min_base=5, step=1, max_base=6)) after E=10 -> 'max_base 6 split of 10: (6,) dust 4'.
confirmed.suggested_fix: When chunking by max_base, choose chunk sizes so that the final remainder is 0 or >= min_valid, for example by balancing ceil(remaining/chunk_cap) equal step-multiple chunks. Mark DUST only if no such partition exists.

verdict.reasoning:
The defect is confirmed at c2b7c6ed9. In cells.py, `_split_valid` (starting at line 811; the reported line 818 is the chunk line) sets `chunk = min(remaining, chunk_cap)` greedily and stops once `remaining < min_valid`. `tp_obligation_to_dispatch` (cells.py:449) and `refresh_dust` (cells.py:506) both count whatever is left after that split as DUST once the entry is final.

At HEAD (09c29d8a4) the later diff only touches cells.py hunks at 583-666, so `_split_valid` is unchanged and a probe against the worktree is valid. I ran one with the test helpers:
- Setup: BUY_CELL entry of 10, fully filled and confirmed terminal, then rules min_base=5, min_notional=0, step=1, max_base=6.
- `tp_obligation_to_dispatch` returned items=(6,), unassigned=10, dust=4.
- `refresh_dust` persisted {0: 4}.
- `state_flags` included DUST.
- `can_release` listed 'DUST' as a blocker.

The split 5+5 is valid under the same rules, so the 4 of DUST was created by the implementation, not forced by the rules.

NG-GRID-003 allows DUST only when "точный остаток меньше runtime minimum" (the exact remainder is below the runtime minimum). Here the exact obligation is 10, which is not below 5. Yet the ledger marks 4 as DUST right away, and AC-33 makes DUST block reset. The spec also forbids adding volume, so the manufactured 4 can never be closed with a valid order. The only way out is aggregation with other lots, if any exist.

On reachability: admission caps the entry at max_base when it is accepted, so this needs max_base to drop at runtime below E, with E mod max_base below the minimum. That is exactly the runtime-rule-change case AC-34 covers, and trading rules are refreshed at runtime. So it is a concrete, reachable path, although a rare one. No test in core/test_cells.py covers a max_base split.

The secondary dust.py:108 point is weaker: the spec says aggregation "допустима" (is permitted), not that it is required. The main cells.py claim stands on its own. Severity low is appropriate.

confirmed.title: AC-39 is claimed done but tested only on a helper the ledger never uses; CellLedger cannot store an aggregate TP or its per-cell allocation
confirmed.requirement: AC-39 (one aggregate TP splits partial fills exactly between cell obligations, idempotently); NG-GRID-003 (the ledger keeps each cell's allocation)
confirmed.failure_scenario: Cell 3, min 5. Gen 0 was released, then late evidence adds a 2 obligation. The entry is final, so refresh_dust makes it DUST 2. Gen 1's entry ends partial and leaves DUST 3. dust.aggregate() builds a valid SELL 5 at the same target, but CellLedger.add_tp_intent(5, generation=g) raises LedgerError 'exceeds unassigned obligation': qty must be <= one cycle's unassigned (cells.py:488-490). AggregateTp.apply_fill returns per-lot deltas, but no CellLedger method applies them to cycle E/X/buckets, and to_record() has no allocation field. The cell stays locked with DUST 5 even though a valid aggregate exists. Any aggregate order WS-D placed could not be reflected in the ledger.
confirmed.evidence: grep finds no use of AggregateTp or dust.aggregate outside dust.py. Tests test_dust.py:47-64 only drive AggregateTp in isolation (per_lot_filled on a local dict). CellLedger.add_tp_intent takes a single generation, and tp_obligation_to_dispatch splits each cycle separately (cells.py:437-456). The trace marks AC-39 'done (logic)'.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Either add a ledger representation for aggregate TP legs (allocation per (cell, generation) persisted in to_record, fills applied through the allocation to each cycle's X) and test it end to end through CellLedger, or downgrade AC-39 in the trace to 'not implemented in ledger' with a WS-D handoff.

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute the claim. It holds against the code at c2b7c6ed9, but it matters less than the reviewer says.

**What I checked**
- **The scenario happens.** I exported c2b7c6ed9 to the scratchpad and drove CellLedger directly:
  1. Gen 0: entry fills 6, gets a terminal proof, TP 6 fills, and the cell is released.
  2. Gen 1 begins.
  3. A late fill of 2 arrives on gen 0's entry and returns LATE_EVIDENCE. The spec expects this case (line 114 and AC-42: late evidence after reuse belongs to the old cycle).
  4. Gen 1's entry fills 5 (TP 5 added), then 3 more, then gets a terminal proof at 8.
  5. After acknowledge_late_evidence(0), refresh_dust returns {0: 2, 1: 3}.
- **The aggregate is valid but the ledger rejects it.** dust.collect finds both lots, and dust.aggregate returns a valid SELL 5 @5.0727 with allocation ((3,0)=2, (3,1)=3). add_tp_intent(5) then raises LedgerError "exceeds unassigned obligation" for generation 0, 1 and None. The check is at cells.py:488-490, and each cycle is capped separately.
- **There is no other way in.** The ledger has no leg type or API for a TP that covers two cycles. apply_fill needs a single TP LegIdentity inside one cycle. Adding each lot as its own TP is also impossible, because 2 and 3 are below the minimum, so order_qty_blocker raises.
- **Allocation is never saved.** to_record()/Cycle.to_record() have no allocation field. AggregateTp (dust.py:125-164) has no persistence and is not referenced anywhere outside dust.py and test_dust.py.
- **WS-D was not told.** The WS-D handoff list in the trace does not mention aggregation at all.

**Spec clause it violates**
NG-GRID-003 (spec line 40) says that when remainders are aggregated, the ledger stores each cell's allocation. AC-39 asks that one aggregate TP split partial fills exactly between the obligations. The trace marks AC-39 "done (logic)", but the only tests are test_dust.py:47-64, which run AggregateTp by itself. No engine built on this ledger can place an aggregate TP, record it or apply its fills, so AC-39 cannot be met end to end.

**Why severity is low, not medium**
- **Rare.** No two cells share a (TP side, target) pair, which test_geometry_no_two_cells_share_tp_side_and_target confirms. So a multi-lot group can only appear after late evidence on a reused cell, which already freezes the market for audit.
- **Optional.** NG-GRID-003 says aggregation is "допустима" (permitted), not required.
- **Safe.** The result is only that the cell stays locked with visible, durable DUST: can_release reports DUST and OLD_CYCLE_OBLIGATION. Nothing is rounded up, no MARKET order is placed and no cap is broken.

The real defect is a lost liveness path plus an overstated AC-39 status in the trace, not a safety violation.

confirmed.title: AC-34 / NG-RISK-005: no test covers rejecting full Q at the TP price after a runtime floor change; dropping that check in admission and begin_entry passes the suite
confirmed.requirement: AC-34 (a new floor blocks invalid submits); NG-RISK-005 (full Q must be valid at the entry price AND the paired TP price; a cell must not be armed into certain permanent DUST)
confirmed.failure_scenario: At runtime, min_notional rises to 54.8. SELL cell 26 has entry 5.4909 (10 x 5.4909 is valid) and TP 5.4727 (10 x 5.4727 < 54.8, invalid). The current code correctly blocks it with FULL_Q_INVALID_TP. But if admission._full_q_blocker or CellLedger.begin_entry checked only the entry price, every test still passes. The cell would be armed, fill 10, and its TP of 10 would be BELOW_MIN_NOTIONAL, leaving the cell in permanent DUST.
confirmed.evidence: Mutations FULLQ_ENTRY_ONLY (admission.py:208-214) and BEGIN_ENTRY_ENTRY_ONLY (cells.py:408-411) each give '110 passed, 87 subtests passed'. The runtime tests use rules(min_base='11') (test_admission.py:101, test_cells.py:383), which fails at both prices, so they cannot tell the TP-leg check apart. Only bootstrap validate_config is tested at the TP price (test_grid.py:117).
confirmed.suggested_fix: Add runtime tests where a floor makes full Q invalid only at the TP price of a SELL cell, e.g. min_notional=54.8 with cell 26. Assert admission.plan blocks it with FULL_Q_INVALID_TP and CellLedger.begin_entry raises.

verdict.reasoning:
The claim holds, but I lowered the severity because the current code behaves correctly.

What I checked. The worktree HEAD is 09c29d8a4, which is later than the reviewed commit and has since changed cells.py, test_cells.py and test_properties.py. So I did not test against HEAD. I used git archive to extract the c2b7c6ed9 snapshot into the scratchpad and ran the core suite there: 110 passed, 87 subtests passed, the same baseline the claim reports. In that scratch copy only, I made three mutations:
- admission._full_q_blocker checks only ENTRY (admission.py:210)
- CellLedger.begin_entry checks only the entry price (cells.py:408)
- both mutations together

Each mutant still gives 110 passed and 87 subtests passed. The original worktree was not changed.

Why no current test catches this. The runtime tests use rules(min_base='11'):
- test_admission.py:101, test_ac34_higher_floor_blocks_new_entries_without_resize
- test_cells.py:383, test_full_q_below_runtime_minimum_is_not_armed

A min_base floor does not depend on price, so Q=10 fails at both legs and these tests cannot tell whether the TP-leg check exists. The TP-only case (cell 27 at min_notional=55) is tested only for bootstrap, in test_grid.py::test_full_q_below_minimum_at_any_entry_or_tp_price_is_rejected_per_cell. That test goes through grid.validate_config, not through the runtime admission and ledger code. test_properties uses min_notional=0, so it does not cover this either.

Why the spec covers it. NG-RISK-005 defines admission as requiring full Q to be valid at both the entry price and the paired TP target, "иначе ячейка не вооружается в заведомо постоянный DUST". It then says a runtime change of minimum, step or notional "повторно валидирует admission и ограничивает новые entries". So the TP-leg check applies at runtime too, not only at bootstrap. The handoff (claude-neutral-grid.md:30) requires tests to be added "до или вместе с каждым инвариантом", i.e. with every invariant. The WS-A trace marks NG-RISK-005 "runtime floors" and AC-34 as done, citing "all of test_admission.py", but no test isolates the runtime TP leg.

The claim's numbers are right: at min_notional=54.8, SELL cell 26 has entry 5.4909 (10 x 5.4909 = 54.909, valid) and TP 5.4727 (10 x 5.4727 = 54.727, invalid).

Why severity is low. This is a gap in test coverage, not a behaviour bug. Both _full_q_blocker and begin_entry do check the TP price today, so the permanent-DUST scenario cannot happen with the current code. It would only happen after a regression, and the suite would not catch that regression.

confirmed.title: AC-57 no-starvation claim unproven: replacing head-of-line queueing with skip-ahead passes the suite
confirmed.requirement: AC-57 (no starvation; queued cells advance deterministically); NG-RISK-005 (queue by distance, then cell_id)
confirmed.failure_scenario: Mutation: in plan(), let later idle cells arm when the head cell does not fit (replace 'head_blocked = True' with 'pass'). The whole suite passes, because every sample cell needs exactly 3 slots, so head-of-line and skip-ahead behave the same. With a floor that makes some TP prices need 4 slots (e.g. min_notional=27, step 0.01: TP 5.5 gives min_valid 4.91, so 4 slots; TP 5.4 gives 5, so 3 slots) and 3 free slots, skip-ahead arms 3-slot cells ahead of the queue head every tick. The head starves indefinitely, and no test detects it.
confirmed.evidence: Mutation SKIP_AHEAD_QUEUE gives '110 passed, 87 subtests passed'. The admission docstring (lines 10-11) claims 'head-of-line (a cell that does not fit blocks the ones behind it, so nothing starves)'. test_ac57 and test_sample_cap_120 only use the uniform 3-slot sample.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Add an admission test with different required_slots per cell, where the head needs more slots than are free. Assert that nothing behind it is newly_armed and that it arms first once the slots free up.

verdict.reasoning:
The claim holds as a test and traceability gap. It is not a runtime defect: the production code is correct.

Code: in admission.py plan(), line 198 sets `head_blocked = True` when the head idle cell does not fit, and line 189 then queues every later cell. This is real head-of-line behaviour. It meets NG-RISK-005 ("Eligible queued cells выбираются по расстоянию ... затем по стабильному cell_id") and AC-57 ("без ... starvation; queued cells продвигаются детерминированно"). admission.py and test_admission.py are identical at c2b7c6ed9 and at the worktree HEAD 09c29d8a4.

Mutation check: I did not touch the worktree. A scratchpad pytest plugin re-executed admission.py with line 198 changed to `pass` (skip-ahead). The whole core suite still passed: 113 passed, 117 subtests passed. The mutation is live in the tested code. I then scanned caps 3..199 using the claim's reachable rules (min_base=0, min_notional=27, step=0.01, Q=10). Some TP prices need 4 slots there and others need 3. With these rules, 20 caps give different newly_armed sets. For example, at cap=9 the original queues head cell 23, while the mutant arms cell 20, which is farther away. This breaks NG-RISK-005 distance ordering and allows starvation. Mixed slot needs are reachable: the spec requires runtime floors, and the handoff forbids hardcoding the 5 LIT minimum.

Tests: test_ac57 (lines 175-179) and test_sample_cap_120 only use the uniform 3-slot sample, so they cannot tell head-of-line from skip-ahead. Even so, trace/ws-a-core.md line 67 marks AC-57 "queue head progresses deterministically" as done using test_ac57. The handoff requires tests alongside each invariant and an AC-to-test matrix that Codex will verify, so this recorded evidence is overstated.

Severity: low, not medium. No wrong behaviour happens at runtime; the gap is only in regression protection and in how accurately the matrix records the evidence. The finding really belongs to test_admission.py and the trace file, not to admission.py:198.

confirmed.title: CidAllocator does not latch on a malformed durable lookup, although its docstring says it does
confirmed.requirement: NG-HIST-004 / AC-43 (fail closed on invalid, colliding or overflowing CIDs; the handoff says 'a latched CidError must drive the engine to DEGRADED')
confirmed.failure_scenario: The durable map returns 2**48 for identity A (a corrupt row). allocate(A) raises CidInvalid, but allocator.failed stays None, and allocate(B) then succeeds and mints CID 1. An engine that relies on the latched 'failed' flag to go DEGRADED keeps submitting with a corrupt CID map. The module docstring (line 8) says a 'malformed value latches the allocator'. The test at test_cid.py:70-71 asserts only the raise, not the latch.
confirmed.evidence: Probe: CidAllocator(exists=lambda c: False, lookup=lambda i: 1<<48 if i.cell_id==0 else None). allocate(cell 0) raises CidInvalid, then failed is None, and allocate(cell 1) returns 1.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Route validate_cid failures from lookup through self._fail(...), and assert alloc.failed is set and later allocations raise.

verdict.reasoning:
The claim is correct, and I reproduced it. In cid.py:73, `known()` calls `validate_cid(found)` on the durable lookup value, and nothing routes that call through `self._fail(...)`. A malformed durable row therefore raises CidInvalid but leaves `self.failed` as None.

Probe: CidAllocator(exists=lambda c: False, lookup=lambda i: 1<<48 if cell 0 else None). allocate(cell 0) raises CidInvalid, `failed` is still None, and allocate(cell 1) then returns 1.

This breaks the module's own contract. Docstring line 8 says a "collision, overflow/exhaustion or malformed value latches the allocator into a failed, fail-closed state". It is also inconsistent inside the same lookup path: a lookup collision does latch, through `_remember` at line 80 (confirmed, `failed` is set). A lookup value that overflows the 48-bit bound does not.

NG-HIST-004 requires overflow, exhaustion and collision to be fail-closed. A durable row of 2**48 is an overflowing value. After it is detected, the allocator keeps minting new CIDs for other legs even though the durable map is known to be corrupt.

The WS-A trace (ws-a-core.md:145) tells the engine integrator that "a latched CidError must drive the engine to DEGRADED". An engine that reads `failed`, or that relies on later allocate() calls failing, would keep submitting. test_cid.py:70-71 checks only the raise, not the latch, so the tests do not catch this.

No engine on any branch (ng-engine, ng-store, and others) uses CidAllocator yet, so nothing elsewhere handles it.

Mitigations: the failing identity itself never gets a new CID, because the lookup re-raises every time. New candidates are still checked with `exists()`, so no duplicate CID is minted. Reaching this path needs a corrupt or buggy durable row. Severity stays low.

confirmed.title: When the venue/user order cap drops, the router still sends TPs from stale per-cell reservations and goes over the cap
confirmed.requirement: NG-RISK-005 (effective max_active_orders/venue cap; slots are never counted twice); NG-RISK-002 (emergency entry cancel is meant for an unexpected venue cap reduction); AC-44; the spec §13.3 property that caps are never violated
confirmed.failure_scenario:
1. One BUY cell is armed with cap=3 and reserves 3 slots. Its entry is live (actual=1).
2. The venue cap drops to 1, so rules.max_active_orders_venue=1.
3. The entry partially fills 5 of 10.
4. admission.plan reports SlotLedger(cap=1, actual=1, reserved_unused=2, free=-2), which is oversubscribed.
5. SlotBudget.from_plan still gives the cell cell_unused=2, and the router returns SUBMIT 'tp:10:0:0' with reason 'OK'.
6. There are now 2 resting orders (the 5-lot entry remainder plus the 5-lot TP) against an effective cap of 1.
7. The AC-44 emergency path (select_entries_to_cancel) never runs, because budget.take never returns None.
8. The venue then rejects the TP for too many orders. That can loop into a new revision on every tick, or the order goes over the user's configured cap.
confirmed.evidence:
router.py:98-110:
- `from_plan` copies `plan.unused(c)` without considering `plan.slots.free < 0`.
- `take()` uses cell_unused before looking at the global pool.

admission.py:141 keeps `reservations[cid] = min(held, targets[cid])` and never shrinks it to fit a reduced eff_cap. On oversubscription, lines 162-164 only set a blocker, which affects entries only.

The property test never lowers the cap: `cap` is fixed per seed in test_properties.py:47, so `len(non_final) <= cap` (line 93) is never tested under a cap drop.

Probe output: 'admission slots: SlotLedger(cap=1, actual=1, reserved_unused=2, free=-2); actions: [SUBMIT tp:10:0:0 OK]; non-final orders now: 2 effective cap 1'.
confirmed.suggested_fix: When plan.slots.free < 0, remove the oversubscription from the unused reservations: cut idle and entry reservations first and exit reservations last, or have SlotBudget.from_plan take the deficit off cell_unused. A TP that cannot fit inside eff_cap then takes the emergency-cancel path: cancel a cap-consuming LIVE entry, wait for history terminal, then submit.

verdict.reasoning:
I confirmed the claim at c2b7c6ed9. The files that matter, router.py, admission.py and contracts.py, are the same at c2b7c6ed9 and at the worktree HEAD (09c29d8a4).

**Code path**
- admission.py:132-141 keeps an open cell's stale reservation, `reservations[cid] = min(max(reserved, actual), target)`. Nothing shrinks it when `eff_cap` falls. On oversubscription, lines 163-164 only set `blocker = SLOTS_OVERSUBSCRIBED`, and that blocker only stops idle cells from being armed (head_blocked).
- router.py:101 `SlotBudget.from_plan` copies `plan.unused(c)` into `cell_unused` and ignores a negative `plan.slots.free`.
- router.py:104-106 `take()` hands out the cell's own reservation before it looks at the global pool.
- So the AC-44 emergency branch at router.py:240-258 (`select_entries_to_cancel`) never runs.

**Probe run against the repo**
1. A BUY cell (Q=10, floor 5) is armed at cap 3 and gets a reservation of 3.
2. The venue cap drops to 1. The entry is LIVE with 5 of 10 filled, and slot_need is 3.
3. Admission gives `SlotLedger(cap=1, actual=1, reserved_unused=2, free=-2)` with blocker `SLOTS_OVERSUBSCRIBED:free=-2`.
4. `SlotBudget.from_plan` gives `SlotBudget(free=-2, cell_unused={10: 2})`.
5. `plan_submits` returns `SUBMIT tp:10:0:0 OK`. That makes 2 non-final orders against an effective cap of 1.
6. With a budget that matches real capacity, `SlotBudget(free=0)`, the same input correctly returns `CANCEL entry (SLOT_EMERGENCY_TP_PRIORITY)` and `WAIT_SLOT:ENTRY_CANCEL_REQUESTED`.

**Spec**
- NG-RISK-002 says emergency cancelling of entries is allowed specifically when the venue order cap drops unexpectedly.
- AC-44 says that when max_active_orders is full, TP priority cancels a cap-consuming entry.
- NG-RISK-005 caps orders at the effective venue cap and says there must be no oversubscription, cancel spam or starvation.
- The code's own docstring for `select_entries_to_cancel` (admission.py:231) says the emergency path is for "venue cap reduced". The stale reservation bypasses exactly that case.

**Tests**
No test lowers the cap at runtime. test_admission only covers a static venue cap, and the property test fixes the cap for each seed. So neither the trace claim "slots never oversubscribed" nor its AC-44 claim covers this case.

**Consequence**
The venue can reject the TP for exceeding the order cap. The obligation then stays, and on the next tick `cell_unused` is still 2, so the router submits again. That is repeated submits and a starved exit, and the emergency cancel never fires. If the venue does not enforce the cap, the effective cap is simply exceeded.

**Scope**
The defect is in router.py and admission.py, which are both in WS-A scope. It is reachable whenever `rules.max_active_orders_venue` shrinks at runtime, which the spec expects can happen. Medium severity is appropriate: it delays or starves an exit and breaks a stated invariant, but it does not directly put the position at risk.

refuted.title: Greedy TP dispatch leaves a permanent DUST lock after a normal two-piece full entry fill in the sample profile
refuted.why:
The behaviour is real, but it follows the spec rather than violating it, and the proposed fix is not dust-free either.

1) The spec requires the greedy dispatch. NG-CELL-002 (spec line 76) says that for each newly confirmed fill the engine immediately adds a TP obligation of the same base quantity. That TP intent must reach the router within 2 s unless a self-trade, cap or minimum blocker applies. A fill of 7 with floor 5 has no minimum blocker, so dispatching TP 7 at cells.py:449-460 is what the spec asks for. Holding back 2 of a valid 7 would delay a dispatchable exit with no spec-listed blocker. AC-05 (2+3+5) only holds a portion that is below the minimum by itself, and the current code passes it (test_ac05_partial_entry_2_3_5_with_floor_5).

2) The clauses cited are not violated.
- NG-GRID-003 (line 40): an exact remainder below the minimum is stored as visible DUST. The remainder 3 < 5 is exactly that case.
- NG-CELL-001 (line 69): condition (4) "no DUST" is an explicit release blocker, so a DUST cell not rearming is the specified behaviour.
- NG-RISK-005 (line 147): this is a bootstrap check that the full Q meets the minimums at both prices. Q=10 with floor 5 passes, so it is not about fill-sequence dust.

3) The claim that a dust-free schedule was available only holds in hindsight. A read-only probe on the same dispatch code (unchanged between c2b7c6ed9 and HEAD) shows:
- Greedy, 7 then +3: dust 3 (confirms the claim).
- Greedy, 7 then the entry is cancelled: dust 0.
- The proposed hold-back, TP 5 with 2 held, then the entry is cancelled: dust 2.

The fix only moves dust from the full-fill path to the cancel path. No policy that cannot see future fills avoids dust in every case, so this is a trade-off the spec does not settle, not a concrete defect.

4) The workstream's trace (ws-a-core.md, Open risks #1 and #2) already records this. It notes that holding back would break the dispatch rule, and that the spec defines no operator path to resolve DUST. That makes it a spec-level gap needing a product decision, not an implementation bug in WS-A.

refuted.title: NG-CELL-004: no test covers the *_TERMINAL_UNKNOWN aggregate states; collapsing them into *_LIVE passes the whole suite
refuted.why:
The code behaves correctly. The claim only describes a gap in the tests. At c2b7c6ed9, CellLedger.state_flags (cells.py:725-753) maps a leg in OrderState.TERMINAL_UNKNOWN to CellState.ENTRY_TERMINAL_UNKNOWN or TP_TERMINAL_UNKNOWN (lines 734-735 and 741-742). Neither state is merged into *_LIVE. _PRIMARY_ORDER (line 755) ranks both unknown states above everything else, so to_view()['state'] shows them first. NG-CELL-004 says the model must not merge states in a way that loses the difference between an intent, an active order and an unknown result, and the code keeps that difference.

The failure scenario only happens if someone changes the code. I confirmed that part of the claim. I patched state_flags in memory, without editing the worktree, so that both unknown states map to *_LIVE. All core tests still pass (113 passed, 117 subtests on the worktree HEAD). No test in core/ checks either aggregate unknown state or SETTLING. A mutation that survives the tests is a test-strength observation, not a reachable wrong result. The brief rules out "consider adding" items and asks for a concrete, reachable scenario. The code in the branch never shows a TERMINAL_UNKNOWN leg as ENTRY_LIVE or TP_LIVE.

The difference is also tested at the leg level. test_cells.py:193 asserts OrderState.TERMINAL_UNKNOWN on the entry leg after a cancel ack. to_view() exposes each leg's state in entry and tp_children. The trace's design note (ws-a-core.md, "Aggregate state is derived") says on purpose that the leg state carries the ambiguity.

The COMPLETE/PAUSED part also does not hold. NG-CELL-004 allows different names ("Названия могут отличаться"). SETTLING is the state for "all legs final, E == X, no dust, not yet released", which is the cycle-complete state. After release the cell returns to IDLE for the next cycle. PAUSED, BLOCKED and QUEUED depend on the engine or the snapshot (EngineState.PAUSED, and the WS-D handoff item 9 adds blocker and queue_age to the snapshot). They are outside the pure core's scope.

The trace marking NG-CELL-004 as "done" with thin aggregate-level tests could be a low-priority note on traceability. It is not an evidenced NG-CELL-004 violation.

refuted.title: Property test never exercises restart ordering or committed-but-unsent intents, which spec 13.3 requires
refuted.why:
The facts in the claim are right, but it points to a test-thoroughness gap, not a reachable defect.

**What checks out.** I ran the INTENT_NOT_COUNTED mutation by monkeypatching `risk.OpenLeg.counts` from a scratchpad script; no repo files were changed.
- `test_properties.py`, `test_risk.py` and `test_router.py` ran 40 tests, and only `test_risk.py::TestCaps::test_ac27_virtual_tp_crosses_zero_non_reduce_only` failed.
- An instrumented `endpoints_from_ledgers` saw exactly one INTENT leg in the whole run, and it came from that AC-27 unit test. The property sweep never has an INTENT leg at a check point, because `CoreSim.tick` records the transport outcome right away (`helpers.py:180-190`).
- `mark_intents_unknown` and a mid-run `from_record` are never used in `random_event`.

**Why it is not a concrete defect.**
1. **The example regression is already caught.** A mutation that drops INTENT legs from the risk endpoints is caught by the AC-27 unit test. The rest is covered elsewhere:
   - The WITHDRAW path for unsent intents is unit-tested in `test_router.py::TestSelfTrade::test_unsent_entry_intent_is_withdrawn_unknown_submit_is_only_waited_for`.
   - The restart transition is unit-tested in `test_cells.py::TestUnknownOutcomes::test_restart_marks_intent_unknown_and_keeps_cid`.
2. **Restart adds no new ledger states for the cap property.** In `cells.py`, the only state `CellLedger` holds is `cycles` and `fills`, and `to_record` writes out every `Leg` and `Cycle` field. So an exact round trip means the restored ledger behaves the same. That round trip is checked on all 60 random end states (`test_properties.py:301-303`) and in `test_record_round_trip_is_exact`.
   - `mark_intents_unknown` only turns INTENT into SUBMIT_UNKNOWN and keeps the CID.
   - `risk.endpoints` counts every non-final leg the same way (`OpenLeg.counts` = not final and `remaining > 0`), so this change has no effect on risk.
   - The sim's `transport=UNKNOWN` toggle already produces the same post-restart state (SUBMIT_UNKNOWN, CID kept, no exchange id). The property test then drives that state through reject, LIVE, fills, cancel and terminal events while checking caps. A "crash after intent commit, then restart" event would reach no ledger or risk state the sweep does not already explore.
3. **The rest of restart ordering belongs to other workstreams.** Crash windows, persisted admission reservations and the outbox are owned by WS-B and WS-D. The store's `fault_hooks` (`before_intent_commit`, `after_intent_commit`, and so on) in CONTRACTS.md, spec §13.2 (fake exchange with crash injection), and handoff items D-3, D-5 and D-6 all say so. The claim's "restored ledger losing reservations" is not possible in core: slot reservations are not ledger state, and the WS-D handoff says to persist `plan.reservations`.

**The trace doc.** Its §13.3 row lists specific invariants and does not claim to test restart ordering. There is no concrete wrong behaviour or cap violation that this gap lets through, so what remains is a "consider adding property events" suggestion, which the review mandate excludes.

refuted.title: AC-44 'unfilled before partially filled' cancel preference is not tested
refuted.why:
This is a test-coverage gap, not a defect. The current behaviour is correct, and the spec does not require the preference the claim is about.

1. **The code already does the right thing.** In admission.py, `select_entries_to_cancel` (lines 227-245) sorts by `(e.filled > 0, -distance, -e.cell_id, e.key)`, so unfilled entries come before partially filled ones. I checked this directly: with a near unfilled entry (5.38, mid 5.4) and a far partially filled one (4.0, filled 5), it returns `('near_unfilled',)`. The failure scenario only happens under a hypothetical future mutation. The current code does not produce it.

2. **The spec does not require the preference.** AC-44 (spec line 342) only says that when `max_active_orders` is full, TP priority cancels a cap-consuming entry, and that TP–TP conflicts go FIFO. The rule "Регулярный partial fill не является причиной отменять entry" (spec lines 58/143) means a regular partial fill is not by itself a reason to cancel an entry. It does not say an emergency slot cancel must skip partially filled entries. Spec line 82 explicitly covers an entry canceled after a partial fill (close the actual cumulative quantity, then start a new cycle), so cancelling a partially filled entry in an emergency is allowed. "Unfilled before partially filled" is an implementation choice, stated in the function's docstring and repeated in the workstream's trace note ("unfilled, farthest"). It is not a spec clause.

3. **Every behaviour the spec does require is tested.** The AC-44 test in test_router.py checks that exactly one cap-consuming entry is cancelled, that the TP then waits without cancel spam, that an in-flight cancel is enough, and that the TP submits once a slot is free. Other tests in the same file (lines 64-68, and test_cells.py:118) check that a partial fill alone never triggers a cancel, which is the actual NG-RISK-002 rule.

The task asks for concrete defects with reachable wrong behaviour and excludes "consider adding" items. A missing test for a correctly implemented, non-mandated tie-break falls outside that. At most it is a low-value note that the trace's "unfilled" wording is not tested.

refuted.title: The fee half of AC-23 is 'proven' by a tautological signature check
refuted.why:
This is a complaint about how strong a test is. It points to no code defect in WS-A, and the failure it describes cannot happen inside this workstream's scope.

1. **Wrong line.** The assertion is at test_cells.py:326-327, inside `test_fees_are_not_an_input_to_base_quantities`, not at line 263.

2. **The core has no fee concept anywhere.** Grepping the core modules (grid, cells, risk, admission, router, cid, dust, contracts) for "fee" finds only the design comment at cells.py:7.
   - `CellLedger.apply_fill` (cells.py:567) takes only `(key, identity, qty, price, side)`.
   - `tp_obligation_to_dispatch` works only from confirmed base E, exit X and reservations.
   - So no path inside WS-A lets a fee enter the TP obligation. The "fee applied in `tp_obligation_to_dispatch` through another path" scenario does not exist.

3. **The test does check behaviour.** The positive assertion (fill 10 gives TP 10, exact) checks the behaviour that matters at core level: the TP equals the exact confirmed base. The `TypeError` check is a cheap structural guard that the ledger API accepts no fee input. It is weak, but it is not wrong.

4. **The remaining scenario is outside WS-A.** A fee-net size passed as `qty` would depend on the WS-C trade-row size and the WS-D history batch, not on WS-A code.
   - The trace's WS-D handoff #4 already says `apply_fill(trade.dedupe_key(domain), identity_from_cid, size, price, own_side)`. That puts the size semantics at the connector/engine boundary.

5. **The overclaim is at most a labelling nit.** Marking AC-23 "done" rather than "core part" is a traceability-label nit. It does not violate NG-*/AC-* and causes no wrong behaviour in this workstream's code. The review brief rules out that kind of finding.

refuted.title: A reject arriving after a recorded timeout frees the reservation and lets the engine mint a new CID/revision
refuted.why:
The failure scenario cannot happen in the system as it is actually wired, and the ledger has to allow the transition it complains about.

1. The contracted protocol needs this transition. The store's `mark_dispatching` moves the leg from INTENT to SUBMIT_UNKNOWN before transport is called (ng-engine worktree, store.py around line 2657-2690, docstring: "Commit 'transport is about to be called'... the leg becomes SUBMIT_UNKNOWN"). The engine's `_dispatch_intent` (engine.py:1598-1615) follows mark_dispatching, then port.submit, then record_transport_result. So the result of the one in-flight call always arrives while the leg is in SUBMIT_UNKNOWN. If cells.py:537-541 refused DEFINITIVE_REJECT_ZERO_FILL from SUBMIT_UNKNOWN, the legitimate NG-DB-005 path (one call, documented definitive zero-fill reject, then a new revision) would break. The claim admits that SUBMIT_UNKNOWN also means "call in flight".

2. The store already enforces "no second result after a recorded timeout". `record_transport_result` (store.py:2723+) looks for an outbox row whose status is not DONE. After a timeout, the row is DONE with outcome UNKNOWN. A later DEFINITIVE_REJECT_ZERO_FILL for that CID finds no open row, does not match the stored outcome, and raises `InvalidTransitionError("no unresolved SUBMIT outbox row...")`. Re-dispatching a DONE/UNKNOWN row needs `resend_same_cid=True`. That flag exists only for documented venue idempotence, which NG-HIST-004 explicitly allows ("Повтор того же ID допустим только при документированной venue idempotence"). Under such idempotence, a definitive reject of the resend is legitimate evidence about that CID. The engine never passes `resend_same_cid`.

3. After a crash, the outbox row stays DISPATCHED and no transport result exists to record. The engine never re-calls transport for such rows; it resolves them through history (`_close_open_outbox` records only UNKNOWN or NOT_SENT). The Lighter connector never emits DEFINITIVE_REJECT_ZERO_FILL at all (lighter_perpetual_derivative.py:1507: "DEFINITIVE_REJECT_ZERO_FILL is never emitted"). The live venue therefore cannot trigger the claimed path.

4. The engine does not call `CellLedger.record_transport`. It mirrors the authoritative store state onto the ledger (`_mirror`, engine.py:463-476). Steps 3-7 of the scenario would need a caller that feeds two transport results for one dispatch. The contract (CONTRACTS.md: one classification per submit_with_client_id call; the outbox is the durable record of the one result) and the store both rule that out.

5. The cited tests model a definitive rejection arriving for a SUBMIT_UNKNOWN leg, which is valid under the in-flight or idempotent-resend meaning. They do not, on their own, show a reachable path that violates AC-56.

At most this is a missing defense-in-depth guard in a pure module that relies on the caller's documented protocol. It is not a concretely reachable violation of NG-HIST-004, NG-DB-005, AC-56 or AC-43.

refuted.title: Proof that a leg marked final-rejected is actually live is swallowed; its remainder leaves P_min/P_max, gross and self-trade checks
refuted.why:
I refuted this claim. The behaviour it describes is real, but neither failure scenario can happen unless another component first breaks its contract, and the one contradiction that can surface in history is already flagged and sent to a market freeze.

**What I reproduced** against c2b7c6ed9, using the package extracted to a scratch directory:
- A 3-lot fill on a REJECTED_ZERO_FILL entry returns LATE_EVIDENCE. The leg stays REJECTED_ZERO_FILL with remaining=7, `endpoints_from_ledgers` gives P_min=P_max=3, and the router's owned set is empty.
- An ACCEPTED result after NOT_SENT leaves the leg in REJECTED_UNSENT, with no flag and an empty `check_invariants()`.

**Why this is not a defect in this workstream**

1. **Case A is already detected and escalated.** The fill sets `leg.late_evidence` and `cycle.late_evidence` (cells.py:589-592). `check_invariants()` then reports "gen0: rejected leg has fills 3" (cells.py:684-685), so the claim is wrong that nothing notices, at least for Case A.
   - `next_entry_identity` and `_can_retry_entry` block any new entry or revision for the cell (cells.py:382-395).
   - The documented handoff (trace ws-a-core.md, WS-D item 4) routes LATE_EVIDENCE to FROZEN, and `CONFLICT_*` outcomes to pause/freeze. That is what the spec requires: AC-40 says an unknown or contradictory owned fill must stop exposure, and AC-42 / NG-HIST late evidence says it freezes the whole market until audit.
   - The claimed harm (a SELL TP slipping past the self-trade check, or a cap breach) needs the engine to keep routing orders while the market is frozen for audit. That would be an engine violation, not a core one.
   - At this commit the invariant error survives `acknowledge_late_evidence`, so an engine that gates on invariants never resumes on the corrupted state either.

2. **The contradiction cannot arise from a correct upstream.** Under NG-DB-005, REJECTED_ZERO_FILL is set only on a documented definitive venue rejection with zero fill. REJECTED_UNSENT is set only with proof that transport was never called. The core admits NOT_SENT only from INTENT (cells.py:534), and INTENT is defined as "transport not yet called" (risk.py:31, `WITHDRAWABLE_STATES`). A later fill on such a leg therefore means the venue or connector (WS-C) misreported, or the engine (WS-D) recorded a false proof. The core already treats that case as a history conflict.

3. **Case B needs an engine bug.** It requires the engine to record NOT_SENT and then receive a transport ACCEPTED for the same send. That breaks WS-D handoff item 3: "record_transport(NOT_SENT) only with proof transport was never invoked". REJECTED_ZERO_FILL followed by ACCEPTED would need two transport results for one send, which cannot happen. Even then, any execution of the hidden order would hit the LATE_EVIDENCE freeze path above.

4. **The spec does not ask for this.** For a history conflict, the spec asks the system to stop exposure and not guess quantities (AC-40). It does not ask the ledger to reopen an order proven final and count its remainder in P_min/P_max. NG-DB-005 explicitly lets a definitive zero-fill rejection count as proven terminal. AC-40 and NG-DB-005 are also outside WS-A's listed scope.

**What is left** is a defence-in-depth preference: moving a rejected leg with contradicting evidence to a non-final state. It is not a concrete failure the core can reach on its own. If it were kept as a finding, it would rate low, not medium.

refuted.title: Greedy TP dispatch knowingly leaves a below-minimum tail as permanent DUST after a fully filled, valid-size entry
refuted.why:
The code does behave as the claim describes. At c2b7c6ed9, cells.py:449 (`_split_valid(unassigned, ...)`) dispatches the whole step-floored unassigned obligation once it reaches min_valid. So with fills 2, 4, 4 it sends TP 6 and later classifies the final 4 as DUST. But the spec does not require the look-ahead hold-back the claim proposes, and the clauses cited do not support it.

1. NG-RISK-005 does not apply. Its "not armed into knowingly permanent DUST" wording (spec line 147) is about bootstrap config admission: the full order_amount_base must be valid at both the entry price and the TP price, otherwise the config is rejected. In this scenario Q=10 with a minimum of 5 passes that check (grid.validate_full_q). The clause says nothing about how later partial-fill TPs are split.

2. The spec expects exactly this kind of dust. NG-CELL-002 says the entry remainder keeps resting "даже если partial remainder меньше текущего minimum". NG-GRID-003 says a remainder below the runtime minimum "сохраняется как DUST и виден оператору". AC-33 only requires that dust is visible and durable and blocks reset, and the implementation does that (test_ac33_dust_is_durable_visible_and_blocks_reset).

3. NG-CELL-002 favours sending the TP right away. For each newly confirmed share, the engine "немедленно добавляет TP obligation того же base quantity" and passes the TP intent to the router within 2 s unless a "self-trade/cap/minimum blocker" exists. When 6 is unassigned there is no minimum blocker: 6 is a valid order, and the extra 1 is not blocked by any minimum. Holding it back is a strategic choice, not a listed blocker. So the claim's reading of the SLO is a stretch, and the implementation follows the text. The trace records this as open risk #1, pending a spec decision.

4. The proposed fix is not strictly better. It holds 1 back while the entry is live. The spec allows a partially filled entry to become terminal without filling fully: router cancels of conflicting entries (AC-31), pause/stop, GTT expiry, and NG-CELL-003's "terminal partial entry". In any of those cases the held-back 1 becomes DUST, where the current code leaves none. It trades one dust scenario for another, so it cannot be a mandated behaviour.

5. The worry that the cell stays locked indefinitely because the spec gives the operator no way to resolve dust is a gap in the spec (trace open risk #2). It is not a defect in this workstream's code, and NG-CELL-001 (4) explicitly requires the lock while dust exists.

This is a documented design trade-off, not a violation of any NG-* or AC-* clause.
